messages:
Maria (Sales): Hey team — AtlasHealth POC. They require strict in-region processing: Canada (ca-central1) + EU (europe-west1) only. BYOK required. Need confirmation we can block any egress to US and a subprocessor list + pricing impact. Can presales + infra + legal weigh in? @Tom @Lee @Jess
Tom (Presales): Short answer: achievable with Dedicated or Private. Hosted API can't guarantee zero US control-plane talk unless we run a regional control plane. Need to clarify telemetry and cert flows.
Lee (Infra): We can pin inference and data-plane to ca/eu zones. For Hosted: control plane defaults to our centralized region (US) unless customer chooses Private (VPC) or Dedicated regional control plane. BYOK supported (HSM-backed) but requires key import procedures and RBAC. Telemetry: we send anonymized metrics from region, but can offer opt-out for POC.
Jess (Legal): We'll need a subprocessor attestation and DPA addendum. If the customer insists on absolute no-US egress, we must document exceptions (CAs, OS package updates, cert revocation checks). Need explicit customer consent if any fallback is allowed.
Sahil (AE): What is the pricing delta for a 6-week POC with these constraints vs our standard free-tier trial? Customer wants a ballpark now.
Tom (Presales): Quick sizing: dedicated regional pool + BYOK + telemetry opt-out/config = approx $12,500/mo for the POC (includes reserved GPU slices + operational support). Private (on-prem/VPC) option is heavier: one-time integration + $8k/mo infra licensing. Numbers are estimates — final after infra sizing.
Maria (Sales): Can you give me a short config snippet I can forward and a short list of what 'no-everywhere' covers vs exceptions? Also they asked about subprocessor names.
Lee (Infra): Config sample (for forwarding):
```yaml
region_pin:
  - ca-central1
  - europe-west1
control_plane: regional-only
byok: true
telemetry_opt_out: true
fallback_policy: "no-fallback"
```
Note: cert validation uses public CAs (OCSP/CRL) which may resolve outside region. We can mitigate by using customer-managed PKI or running a local CA proxy, but that adds ~1 week infra work.
Tom (Presales): Regarding subprocessors: primary cloud provider (GCP) in EU/CA regions, our monitoring vendor (regionally hosted options), KMS/HSM vendor (customer-managed or regional partner). Lee will provide a region-scoped export.
Jess (Legal): I'll draft the attestation template and DPA addendum. If AtlasHealth requires no fallback, we need an explicit acceptance of risks for cert/CA flows in the addendum.
Lee (Infra): Action: I'll generate the subproc export and a short note on telemetry egress points (expected within 48 hours). Also callout: regional dedicated pools incur ~15% cost uplift vs multi-region pooled capacity.
Sahil (AE): Timeline question — if SOW signed this week, can we stand up the POC in 3 weeks? Customer is sensitive to calendar.
Tom (Presales): Tentatively yes: 1 week to provision dedicated pool & BYOK setup, 1 week for infra config and cert/PKI mitigation, 1 week customer onboarding + smoke tests. POC runtime 2-4 weeks depending on customer cadence.
Maria (Sales): I'll check with AtlasHealth and confirm 'no-fallback' (they said they'd try to accept cert mitigation). Will update here once they sign SOW. Thanks all :thumbsup:
routing-bot: Reminder: created INFRA-8932 for telemetry opt-out and assigned to Lee.
